items.title: The Sea Has the Answers review: Confronting privilege and personal awakening
items.summary: When public accusations of sexual misconduct break out, media coverage often centres on two primary nodes: the brave survivors stepping forward, and the fall of the accused person. Rarely do narratives slow down to examine the murky, collateral space occupied by the family left in the wake of such revelations. In The Sea Has the Answers , journalist-author Shuma Raha sets out to explore this exact terrain. The novel opens with Urmimala Das, a woman whose upper-crust, comfortable life in Kolkata collapses overnight when her high-profile advertising executive husband, Shankar, is outed during a #MeToo wave. Retreating to Kinjalka, her ancestral home by the Bay of Bengal, Urmi attempts to process the dissolution of her marriage, her own blindness to her husband's behaviour, and her fractured sense of self. On paper, Raha’s premise offers a vital lens into structural patriarchy, institutional protection of powerful men, and the lingering social ripples of #MeToo.
